players.comment: McCollum (calf) will miss at least four weeks, per Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network. The veteran combo guard has been diagnosed with a left calf strain, and he's in line to miss the next month or so. Once rookie first-rounder Kingston Flemings (back) is healthy, he'll have a long runway as Atlanta's top point guard. Aaron Wiggins remains worth holding in nearly all fantasy leagues as well.

McConnell (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. After missing Indiana's past two games with left hamstring soreness, McConnell joined the club's G League affiliate for practice Tuesday. The veteran point guard can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Philadelphia until the Pacers provide an update on his progress.

Nance exited Monday's game against the Thunder due to a sore right ankle and he will not return, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Nance will have three full days to rest his sore ankle before the Pacers' next game, although with Friday's matchup with the 76ers being the first of a back-to-back set, Nance may need to miss that one as well. Obi Toppin figures to pick up most of Nance's minutes while he's sidelined.

Prince underwent arthroscopic right knee surgery Nov. 18 and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports. Prince last appeared in a game for Detroit on Nov. 14 and is now set to miss an extended period as he recovers from knee surgery. However, the veteran forward's absence shouldn't significantly impact Detroit's rotation.

Nurkic (foot) has been cleared for on-court work and will be re-evaluated in one week. Nurkic continues to make progress in his recovery from a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe on his right foot, and getting cleared for on-court work is a big step in his rehab. There are still a few steps he'll need to clear before he makes his return to the floor, but once he's able to get through full-contact, 5-on-5 work, we'll know he's close.
Landale (hip) won't play Sunday against the Pistons. This will be Landale's fourth consecutive game on the inactive list. His next chance to play will come Friday in Boston.

Robinson (quadriceps) is considered day-to-day as he progresses in his rehab, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports. Robinson will miss a fifth consecutive contest Tuesday due to a left quadriceps strain, though he can be considered questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee until the Pistons provide an update on his status. Kevin Huerter will likely continue seeing increased playing time for as long as Robinson is sidelined.

Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis. This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

Brown (hamstring) won't return to Wednesday's game against Miami, Kyle Neubeck of AllPHLY.com reports. He finished with six points (2-8 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound and one assist over 17 minutes. Brown appeared to grab his left hamstring toward the end of the second quarter and checked out nearly immediately. Considering he recently missed two games because of the ailment, it wouldn't be surprising if he didn't suit up Friday in Indiana. In the meantime, Dean Wade will start the second half, with Kentavious Caldwell-Pope and Anfernee Simons in line for more minutes.

players.comment: Isaac (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Wizards. Isaac continues to deal with a knee injury that has kept him out of action for the entire 2026-27 season. He should continue to be considered week to week until the Magic offer an update on his recovery process.

Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

Reaves (heel) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Daniel Starkand of LakersNation.com reports. Reaves has missed the last five games with a left heel contusion but is trending in the right direction ahead of Friday's game at San Antonio. The Lakers will provide an update on his status by Thursday night, and the 28-year-old shooting guard's return would leave fewer minutes available for Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton and Jake LaRavia.

Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN. Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

Robinson (illness) is out for Tuesday's game against Washington, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports. With Robinson set to miss a third contest due to an illness, Boston will again be without one of its primary center options. His absence should continue to leave more frontcourt minutes available for Neemias Queta and Luka Garza on Tuesday, with the former being in line to see the lion's share of the playing time.

Barrett has been diagnosed with a right hamstring strain and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports. Based on his re-evaluation timeline, Barrett likely won't return to game action until mid-December at the earliest. Jamison Battle, Allen Graves and Jamal Shead are candidates for increased playing time in Barrett's absence, especially while Kawhi Leonard (knee) is also sidelined.

Nesmith is out for Monday's game against the Thunder due to right foot soreness. The swingman is sitting out the second leg of this back-to-back set and is likely facing a short-term absence. Nesmith's absence should get Obi Toppin onto the streaming map in fantasy leagues Monday.

Haliburton (hamstring) was recalled from the G League's Noblesville Boom on Tuesday, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Haliburton joined the Pacers' G League affiliate for practice Tuesday, taking a significant step forward in his recovery from a left hamstring strain. However, Shams Charania of ESPN reported Friday that the star point guard is expected to miss at least two more weeks, so Haliburton isn't expected to return to game action in the near future.

players.comment: Hayes (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Lakers. Hayes left Sunday's tilt against the Mavericks with what's now being described as a left knee strain, and it's not yet known how much time he may miss beyond Monday. Mo Bamba should start at center for the Jazz and is worthy of streaming consideration in all fantasy leagues.

Watford (ankle) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs. Watford can be considered week-to-week at this point until the Pelicans offer an update on his recovery. He hasn't played since Nov. 8 and is averaging just 7.2 points and 3.5 boards per game in his six appearances off the bench.

Cunningham (knee) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Orlando. Cunningham was listed as probable, so his absence for Tuesday's meeting with the Magic is concerning. Head coach J.B. Bickerstaff indicated that the knee has been giving the two-time All-Star some trouble of late, and while he's mostly played through it, he will now miss his second game of the 2026-27 campaign. Without Cunningham, Isaiah Joe will enter the starting lineup.

The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks. Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports. Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

Bittle (foot) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Bucks, Blake Murphy of Sportsnet.ca reports. Bittle continues to work his way back from a fractured right foot, as he's yet to make his 2026-27 season debut. He remains week-to-week until Toronto provides a definitive update.

Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic. The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

Duren (hamstring) is being assigned to the Motor City Cruise on Wednesday for practice as he ramps up for a return, Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com reports. With Duren still out for Detroit and now progressing to a G League practice assignment, this marks a tangible step forward in his recovery from the right hamstring strain that has kept him sidelined since Oct. 23. The Pistons haven't provided a return timeline, but his return appears to be drawing closer as he increases his activity.

The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL. Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

Mathurin (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Thunder. Mathurin will miss a fourth straight contest due to plantar fasciitis in his left foot, which tends to be a lingering injury. Jordan Poole should remain in the backcourt rotation for the undermanned Pelicans moving forward, while Mathurin can be deemed week-to-week.

Head coach Dusty May said Friday that Lively (foot) is moving well and progressing in his recovery, and the big man told May he's "close" to returning, Mike Curtis of The Dallas Morning News reports. Lively hasn't seen game action since Nov. 21, 2025, and he remains without a firm timetable to return after undergoing right foot surgery last December. However, this update suggests that the big man is trending in the right direction.

The Pelicans transferred Reese from the G League's Laketown Squadron, and he will be available for New Orleans' game against the Warriors on Monday. Reese dropped a 15-point, 15-rebound double-double in the Squadron's win over the Mexico City Capitanes on Saturday and will return to the parent club ahead of its game Monday. Through five regular-season appearances at the NBA level this season, the big man is averaging 1.2 points and 1.0 rebounds in 5.4 minutes per tilt.

Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

Newell underwent surgery Tuesday for a plantar plate tear in his left great toe, and he will be re-evaluated in approximately four months, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports. Newell suffered the toe injury in the Nov. 4 win over Washington and is now set to miss an extended period. With Mouhamed Gueye (foot) expected to miss at least three more weeks, Aaron Wiggins and Corey Kispert could see a slight bump in minutes moving forward.

Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Boston. Vukcevic has yet to suit up this season due to a left hip injury. He can be considered week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday. Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.
Lawal (groin) is out for Tuesday's game against Denver. Lawal is slated for a fourth consecutive absence due to a right groin strain. His next opportunity to return will arrive Friday in Phoenix.

Head coach Sean Sweeney said Wednesday that Nelson (ankle) has been doing "some on-court stuff," though Sweeney added that the work has been "minimal," Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Nelson underwent surgery this offseason to repair a fractured left ankle. It's encouraging to hear that he's made some progress, but the two-way player can still be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Biberovic (heel) is out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. Biberovic has yet to debut for the Mavs this season due to a right heel bursitis issue, and the fact that he continues to get ruled out a full day in advance of tipoff suggests he's still not close. Biberovic should be considered week-to-week moving forward.

Penda (hamstring) is making progress but remains without a timetable to return to game action, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports. Penda suffered a partially torn hamstring in the preseason and can still be considered week-to-week moving forward. With the second-year forward and Paolo Banchero (ankle) both sidelined, Tristan da Silva and Jamal Cain should continue seeing increased minutes.

The Pistons announced Tuesday that Okorie (oblique) will miss at least two weeks, per Eric Vincent of ClutchPoints.com. Okorie has been diagnosed with an oblique strain, which he sustained in a G League game. The rookie first-rounder has logged a grand total of 20 minutes across five brief appearances, so his absence doesn't have major fantasy ramifications.

De Larrea (knee) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Warriors. De Larrea has only played four games during the 2026-27 campaign. There hasn't been any indication of when he will be cleared to return, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

Leonard has begun individual on-court workouts following treatment to address swelling in his left knee, and he will be re-evaluated in one week, Marc J. Spears of ESPN.com reports. Leonard continues to progress in his recovery, and the Raptors are expected to provide another update in a week. Collin Murray-Boyles and Allen Graves will likely continue seeing increased burn for as long as Leonard is sidelined.
